items.note: A 38-line inscription at Paratheda records the foundation and endowment of the Mandaleśa Śiva temple, dated V.S. 1116 (A.D. 1059); royal foundation records give builders, artisans, composer, date and endowment (comparison, not Udaypur).
The Nīlakaṇṭheśvara, representing the Bhūmija style in fully developed form, was completed in A.D. 1080.
Nīlakaṇṭheśvara compared with Chaubara Dera No. 1: more vedibandha mouldings, a band of images in one row on the jaṅghā, and lotus scrolls on the salilāntaras.
Mandapa plan of the Nīlakaṇṭheśvara is elaborate: a gūḍhamaṇḍapa with dvāramaṇḍapas on two sides, with kakṣāsanas, entrances and dvārapālas.
The Udaypur Praśasti says Bhoja, a zealous devotee of Śiva, covered the world with temples to Kedāra, Rāmeśvara, Somanātha, Sundira, Kāla, Anala and Rudra.
Following the Bhūmija prāsāda precepts laid down in the Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra, Bhoja probably began construction of temples mostly dedicated to Śiva (citing Bhatia).
Bhojaśālā at Dhārā had inscribed alphabetical charts and grammatical rules within twin snake coils, called Sarpabandha inscriptions.
